paragraphs: Sam, Mia, and Pat are in the park. Sam has his new skates. The sun is hot, and the sky is blue. "I can skate, and I'm quick!" he says. Mia looks at him. "I can't skate," she says. "But I can run very quickly." Pat has a ball. "Can I kick it?" asks Pat. He kicks the ball into the net and scores.

Then Mia sees something on a big rock. It is small and brown. "Look!" she says. "It's a bat!" The bat is on the rock, and it is not happy. "Why can't it fly?" asks Pat. "Is it ill?" asks Mia. Sam looks at the bat carefully. "Its leg is hurt," he says. "It can't fly today."

"We can help it," says Mia. Mia has an old cage at home. "I can't climb the rock," says Pat. "I can," says Sam. He climbs the rock and holds the bat carefully. The bat is very quiet. It looks at us with big, dark eyes. The children put it in the cage. Mia's mom calls an animal doctor. "Now the bat can sleep," says Mia. "One day it can fly again."
text.summary: Sam, Mia, and Pat play in the park. Mia finds a small bat that can't fly, and the children help it.
